# Saturated liquid molar volume from the COSTALD equation

`eos.costald_molar_volume`

## Equation

$$
V_s = V^{*}\,V_R^{(0)}\,(1 - \omega V_R^{(\delta)})
$$

In the form the library evaluates:

```python
v = V* * V_R0 * (1 - omega*V_Rdelta),  V_R0 = 1 - 1.52816*tau**(1/3) + 1.43907*tau**(2/3) - 0.81446*tau + 0.190454*tau**(4/3),  V_Rdelta = (-0.296123 + 0.386914*Tr - 0.0427258*Tr**2 - 0.0480645*Tr**3)/(Tr - 1.00001),  tau = 1 - Tr
```

## Source

**Hankinson, R. W.; Thomson, G. H. (1979)**

A new correlation for saturated densities of liquids and their mixtures. AIChE J., 25(4), 653-663

DOI: [10.1002/aic.690250412](https://doi.org/10.1002/aic.690250412)

## Inputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `omega` | dimensionless | Acentric factor of the pure component. |
| `Tc` | K | Critical temperature of the pure component. |
| `Vc` | m**3/mol | Critical volume; the characteristic-volume fallback when no normal liquid density is supplied. |
| `M` | kg/mol | Molar mass, for the characteristic-volume back-calculation. |
| `rho_normal` | kg/m**3 | Normal liquid density at 288.71 K; zero when unknown, in which case `Vc` is the characteristic volume. |
| `T` | K | Absolute temperature, below the critical temperature. |


## Outputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `v` | m**3/mol | The saturated liquid molar volume at `T`. |


## Valid range

| Bound | On violation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `Tc > 0` | raises | `Tc` is the divisor in `Tr = T/Tc`; zero or negative is not a critical temperature. |
| `Vc > 0` | raises | A critical volume is positive; a non-positive value is not a substance. |
| `T > 0` | raises | An absolute temperature; zero and below are not states. |


## Assumptions

These are **not** checked at runtime. They are what the caller has to
satisfy for the result to mean what it says.


- the acentric factor, critical constants, molar mass and normal liquid density are those of the component intended. NOT CHECKED - they come from the caller.

- the characteristic volume `V*` is back-calculated from the normal liquid density at 288.71 K, falling back to the critical volume when the density is absent or the reduced standard temperature reaches 0.9 - the same order NeqSim's `getCharacteristicVolume` follows.

- the volume is the *saturated* liquid molar volume; the Aalto compressed-liquid correction and the NASTALD polar correction are not applied here (the latter is name-based and belongs to a later model).

- the correlation is valid below the critical temperature; above it the saturated volume is undefined.




## Worked example

Source: derived from the equation above

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| `omega` | 0.3013 |
| `Tc` | 507.6 |
| `Vc` | 0.00037 |
| `M` | 0.086177 |
| `rho_normal` | 664.0 |
| `T` | 298.15 |

| Output | Expected |
|---|---|
| `v` | 0.0001315006475383877 |

Relative tolerance: `1e-12`

n-hexane, omega = 0.3013, Tc = 507.6 K, Vc = 3.7e-4 m**3/mol, M = 0.086177 kg/mol, rho_normal = 664 kg/m**3, at T = 298.15 K: Tr_std = 288.71 / 507.6 = 0.5687746256895192 V_R0(Tr_std) = 0.37770057227628073 V_Rdelta(Tr_std) = 0.2289284633940725 factor = 0.37770057227628073 * (1 - 0.3013*0.2289284633940725) = 0.35164824245087495 V_molar_std = 0.086177 / 664 = 0.00012978463855421688 m**3/mol V* = 0.00012978463855421688 / 0.35164824245087495 = 0.00036907518049758976 m**3/mol Tr = 298.15 / 507.6 = 0.5873719464144995 V_R0 = 0.38235768189745517 V_Rdelta = 0.22620631480355938 v = 0.00036907518049758976 * 0.38235768189745517 * (1 - 0.3013*0.22620631480355938) = 0.0001315006475383877 m**3/mol which, with n-hexane's M, is rho = 655.34 kg/m**3 - the NIST value.
